items.title: Verstappen wins; McLaren secure a double podium
items.summary: Verstappen beat Norris by 0.639 seconds and Piastri by 1.529. Mercedes had contested the lead, but Russell fell to ninth late and Antonelli to fourth.
items.why_it_matters: Use the official result and keep the late Mercedes drop specific to Las Vegas rather than treating it as a Qatar forecast.

sources.label: Formula1.com race report, full article checked

items.title: Vasseur calls Leclerc–Hamilton clash 'unacceptable'
items.summary: After a Turn 7 collision, Leclerc accepted blame; team principal Fred Vasseur called it 'unacceptable' and 'a lack of respect', two races after another clash in Mexico. Formula1.com's reports differ on whether it was Lap 37 or Lap 38, so no lap number is given. The FIA Doc 54 versus final Doc 65 sanction-footnote mismatch remains unresolved on the Penalties and Notes pages.
items.why_it_matters: This is a continuing team-relations story for Qatar; keep the FIA record discrepancy visible and do not imply that Ferrari has announced new team orders.

sources.label: FIA Document 60, visually checked; Turn 7 collision ruling

items.title: Perez has a five-place drop at his next race
items.summary: The stewards found Perez wholly responsible for contact with Câmara at Turn 14. Because Perez retired, the unserved time penalty was converted to a five-place drop at his next race.
items.why_it_matters: Qatar is the expected next application. This is a grid penalty, not a five-second race penalty, and the Vegas PU sanctions must not be carried over a second time.

items.title: Hadjar's front wing fails; a separate Safety Car penalty demotes him
items.summary: Hadjar reached the lead battle before his front wing collapsed; he said he did not know the cause. A separate 10-second penalty for driving unnecessarily slowly behind the Safety Car dropped him to 15th.
items.why_it_matters: Keep the wing-failure cause unconfirmed and distinguish it from the Safety Car infringement.

items.title: Wolff says Antonelli lost battery power in the closing laps
items.summary: Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said Antonelli lifted behind Verstappen before reapplying, leaving him with no battery on the back straight; both McLarens passed and Antonelli finished fourth. Wolff said Mercedes had planned an energy deployment for the final 400 metres that could have offered a chance to win.
items.why_it_matters: Keep this attributed to Wolff's post-race account, not independent telemetry or Qatar's published FIA limits; it is Las Vegas context, not a Qatar prediction.
